//: Lighthouse CI config — §10.9 / §7 FE quality gates.
//audited_pages: Six representative surfaces covering the unauth entry, the post-auth shell, the live-data /runs surface, the knowledge surfaces, and settings. Protected routes are gated by the §5.7.1 layout; in mock mode the guard is client-side and the page still renders (auth check runs after first paint), which is what Lighthouse needs to audit. In live mode the gate would 302 to /login pre-paint, which Lighthouse follows transparently.
//thresholds: perf 0.80 / a11y 0.90 / best-practices 0.85 / seo warn-at-0.85. WCAG-critical audits (color-contrast, image-alt, label, link-name) are errored individually so an a11y regression on a single rule fails the gate even if the rolled-up category score stays above 0.90. SEO is warn-only because protected routes are noindex by design.
//start_command: We run lhci against `pnpm start` (the standalone production build) rather than `pnpm dev` — turbopack-dev adds HMR overhead that skews perf scores and makes runs noisier. The CI workflow boots `next start` and waits for :3000 before invoking lhci; lhci itself does not need to start the server.
